content:
Apple TV has long been hailed as the "new HBO," winning on quality over quantity. However, in recent months, the streaming platform has aggressively expanded its lineup to the point where it's impossible to keep up.

Apple TV enters a new era, with quality and quantity rising in tandem

I've been subscribed to Apple TV since its 2019 launch, and at any given time, there's usually only one or two shows on the platform that I genuinely want to watch.

This production model is very similar to HBO — HBO built its brand by producing a small number of generally high-quality series, beating most of its rivals in the process.

However, over the past few years, Apple has gradually increased output while seemingly raising the quality bar even further.

The result is that Apple now has too many great shows airing simultaneously for me to keep up with.

Below are the Apple TV series currently airing new episodes every week:

  • Ted Lasso — one of my personal favourites
  • Slow Horses — another all-time classic in Apple's library
  • Dark Matter — a sci-fi series whose first season I loved, though I haven't started the second yet
  • Brothers — a new half-hour sitcom starring Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson; looks pretty entertaining
  • Last Seen — a new thriller that I've heard great things about but haven't watched yet
  • There's also Women in Blue and Knife Edge Edge, which I might save for when I'm less busy — but for now they're lower on the list

I really want to start Dark Matter, because the first season already elevated it to one of my all-time favourite sci-fi shows, just behind Severance and Pluribus. But it's really hard to find the time to begin the second season. And half-hour sitcoms are always my go-to comfort viewing, so Brothers is already lined up next.

I enjoy crime thrillers and family-themed shows, so Last Seen is right up my alley. But even with the Stephen King stamp of approval, I still haven't started it.

And the above is only what's currently airing.

Silo — I haven't even finished the third season yet, and I haven't even opened Sugar Season 2, despite the rave reviews and the fact that I loved the show myself. If I dropped all my other streaming services, I'd obviously have far more time for Apple's offerings, but shows on other platforms are eating up plenty of my time too.

October is almost here, and Apple is about to drop seven brand-new series and films all at once — the most in a single month I can recall.

All in all, I'm genuinely excited about what Apple TV is doing right now. It's no fluke that Apple has won more Emmys than HBO this year.

What are your thoughts on Apple TV's recent and current lineup? Feel free to share in the comments below.

Apple TV costs US$14.99 per month, with discounts available through the Apple One bundle subscription.
